title: sre-weekly-ops-sync-notes-2026-03-13-draft
body:
Weekly ops sync + reliability review (draft notes)

Attendees: Samira (owner), Evan, Marta, Noah, oncall (David)
Date: 2026-03-13
Context: quick sync before platform review on Friday. Focus on recent SLO regressions, paging trends, and two top incidents from last week.

Agenda:
- Quick SLO snapshot
- Paging trends / noise breakdown
- Top incidents + short postmortem status
- Action items and owners
- AOB (release window, driver update, next oncall rota)

SLO snapshot (high level):
- generation-api (prod, global): availability target 99.95% (rolling 30d)
  - Current 30d availability: 99.93% (down from 99.97% two weeks ago)
  - Error budget burn: ~18% remaining for the 30d window
- p99 latency (short prompts, <=128 tokens): target <300ms
  - Current p99: 480ms (spike correlated with dedicated pool pressure, see SRE-1419)
  - p95 ~ 210ms (unchanged)
- embeddings endpoint: availability and latency within SLOs

Notes: the main regression is p99 for generation. p95 stable -> indicates tail latency issue, likely queuing / OOM fallback on some nodes.

Paging trends (last 14 days):
- Pages to oncall up 35% week-over-week.
- Top page sources:
  1) generation worker OOMs (SRE-1419) -> noisy during model rollouts / quant profile change
  2) transient CUDA driver crashes after node maintenance (SRE-1423)
  3) increased 5xx from transformer runtime when cache misses + batch spikes occur
- Noise analysis: ~40% of pages are duplicates for the same underlying incident (alerts not deduping across AZs). Need dedupe/change to alert grouping or correlate by incident id.

Top incidents (summary):
- SRE-1419: "generation nodes OOM after quantization profile change"
  - Impact: elevated p99 latency, ~30m degradation window for customers on Dedicated pools in us-west-2; ~2% error rate increase during incident
  - Root cause (prelim): new quant profile reduced memory headroom on some 80GB GPUs when handling long-context requests with KV cache; fallback behavior caused workers to retry and queue leading to tail latency
  - Mitigation: rolled back quant profile on affected pool at 2026-03-09 15:32 UTC; auto-scaling temporarily increased worker count for pool
  - Follow-ups: add pre-deploy consistency test for memory usage and a canary job that runs long-context workload on dedicated pools
  - Owner (postmortem): Evan Li

- SRE-1423: "inference worker crashes after CUDA driver update"
  - Impact: intermittent process crashes during node maintenance; required rolling restart, ~45m total degraded capacity in one AZ
  - Root cause: incompatible minor driver change + missing graceful restart hook in worker supervisor config
  - Mitigation: pinned driver version on nodes, forced supervisor restart order to avoid thundering herd
  - Follow-ups: update node maintenance runbook and add canary nodes to maintenance pipeline
  - Owner (postmortem): Marta Rodriguez

Action items (tracked):
- [ ] (High) Add memory regression test to CI that simulates long-context KV cache usage across quant profiles. Owner: Evan. Due: 2026-03-20. Linked: PR referenced above.
- [ ] (High) Implement alert dedupe/grouping by pool+incident id to reduce duplicate pages. Owner: Noah. Due: 2026-03-27. Linked: JIRA SRE-1435 (create ticket).
- [ ] (Medium) Update node maintenance runbook to include driver compatibility check + staged rollouts. Owner: Marta. Due: 2026-03-18.
- [ ] (Medium) Add canary job that continuously exercises dedicated pools with long-context requests (nightly). Owner: Samira. Due: 2026-03-24.
- [ ] (Low) Revisit p99 alert threshold to avoid alert storms from short-lived spikes; tweak to require sustained breach >5m. Owner: David (oncall). Due: 2026-03-16.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should we increase default node memory headroom for Dedicated pools for two weeks after model changes? Pro: buys time during rollouts; Con: increases cost. (tentative: allow as temporary policy for major quant/profile updates)
- Canary failure policy: if canary fails, should we auto-block rollout or just alert? (proposal: block major rollout for 1h if canary fails)

Quick TODOs for next sync:
- Bring updated traffic/latency charts (Evan) — include per-pool p99 breakdown
- Present draft memory regression CI job (Evan + runtime team)
- Update on progress for alert dedupe (Noah)
- Confirm maintenance runbook updates (Marta)

Notes to self:
- Mention cost tradeoff to product (short email) if we propose temporary headroom bump
- Remind release engineering to coordinate driver upgrades with SRE two days prior to window

Meeting adjourned. Next sync: 2026-03-20 (same time).

---
Scratchpad / extra logs:
- Raw alerts sample: ALERT generation-worker-oom pool=dedicated-us-west-2 instance=i-0abc123 2026-03-09T15:10Z
- Quick grep output from logs: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory" x 143 during 15:05-15:40 UTC
- Temp notes for postmortem: include timeline, customer impact table, mitigation runbook steps, lessons learned, owners for each follow-up

End of notes.
